titleText.es: Pero, por favor, confirma que soy realmente *yo* el que está en Klout, y no ninguno de mis amigos intentando que me den un puñetazo. Lo bueno de este pedal de hombre muerto es que nunca me atreveré a activarlo.
titleText.en: Though please do confirm that it's actually *me* on Klout first, and not one of my friends trying to get me punched. The great thing about this douchebag deadman switch is that I will never dare trigger it.
titleText.noteEn: The Spanish archive and official xkcd #1057 title attributes are preserved exactly. KLOUT is the unchanged service name and is audited as non-Spanish text. The raster wraps PEDIR- / TE as one lexical word PEDIRTE; its line-wrap hyphen is punctuation. OCR dropped many initial letters, including those in QUIERO, MOMENTO, FUTURO, ENCONTRAMOS, IGNORA, RETRACTACIÓN, and the request rows, so the authored transcript and direct bounds follow the raster rather than the recognized strings.

applications.explanationEn: Te is attached to the dictionary form pedir and identifies one familiar person as the person being asked.
Pedirte combines the request action with the familiar recipient marker te, and un favor names the requested help.

regions.labelEs: SI EN ALGÚN MOMENTO DEL FUTURO NOS ENCONTRAMOS

applications.exampleEs: SI EN ALGÚN MOMENTO DEL FUTURO NOS ENCONTRAMOS
applications.explanationEn: Si introduces this genuinely possible future condition, the middle words locate the possible meeting in time, and nos encontramos remains in the ordinary present form.
En, algún, and momento form the fixed time expression for an unspecified point.

regions.labelEs: Y SI, EN ESE MOMENTO, HE INTERACTUADO CON KLOUT PARA OTRA COSA QUE NO SEA BORRARME,

excludedUnits.rationale: Klout is the unchanged proper name of the online influence-scoring service, not Spanish lexical vocabulary.

applications.exampleEs: SI, EN ESE MOMENTO, HE INTERACTUADO
applications.explanationEn: Si introduces a possible future condition; he is the present helper and interactuado completes the present-perfect verb inside that condition.
He is the first-person present helper and interactuado is the unchanged completed-action form.
Interactuado supplies the completed interaction action, and con introduces the service involved.
Otra cosa leaves the alternative unspecified, que begins its description, and no sea uses the special non-factual form because no established alternative is being identified.
Me is attached to borrar to mark the speaker as the person removing his own entry or account.

regions.labelEs: QUIERO QUE ME DES UN PUÑETAZO EN LA CARA, SIN AVISAR.

applications.explanationEn: Quiero que introduces an action wanted from another person, and des is the special wanted-action form of dar for one familiar listener.
Me marks the recipient, des supplies the requested form of dar, and un puñetazo names the blow.
Sin is followed directly by the unchanged dictionary form avisar to describe the action that is not done.

regions.labelEs: SI ESTO TE SUENA A BROMA, ACLARO:

applications.explanationEn: Si introduces the possible interpretation, and suena stays in the ordinary present form; esto and te name what creates the impression and for whom.
Suena supplies the impression, a is the required link, and broma names what it resembles.
En and serio form the fixed expression that marks the preceding statement as genuine rather than a joke.

regions.labelEs: IGNORA CUALQUIER RETRACTACIÓN QUE PUEDA HACER.

applications.explanationEn: Ignora is the affirmative tú command for one familiar listener.
Cualquier comes before the singular noun retractación to leave the possible retraction unspecified.
Cualquier retractación does not identify one known retraction, que begins its description, and pueda uses the special non-factual form for a merely possible one.
Pueda carries the person and possibility form, while hacer remains in its unchanged dictionary form.

cards.answerEn: to ask you for; to request from you
cards.noteEn: Pedirte combines pedir, 'to ask for,' with te, which marks one familiar person as the person being asked. Te is attached because pedir is in its unchanged dictionary form.

example.en: I want to ask you for some advice.

cards.promptEs: verbo en forma de diccionario + pronombre unido
cards.questionEn: Where can a short object word such as me, te, lo, or la go with an unchanged action verb?
cards.answerEn: Attach it to the end of the verb and write the result as one word.
cards.noteEn: An unchanged dictionary-form verb ends in -ar, -er, or -ir. Short object words can attach directly: conocer + te becomes conocerte, and ayudar + me becomes ayudarme.

example.en: I want to help you.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone asks another person for a favor?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of pedir, mark the person being asked with me, te, le, nos, os, or les, and add un favor.
cards.noteEn: Pedir changes for the person and time. The short word marks who receives the request: te pido or pedirte for one familiar person, for example. Favor names the requested act of help.

example.es: Voy a pedirle un favor a Marta.
example.en: I am going to ask Marta for a favor.

cards.questionEn: How do you introduce a real or possible condition with “if”?
cards.answerEn: Use si without an accent, followed by an ordinary present-time verb form.
cards.noteEn: This pattern treats the condition as genuinely possible. Spanish normally does not put a future-tense verb directly after si in this kind of condition; the result can appear separately as a statement, prediction, or command.

example.en: If you have time, call.

cards.answerEn: at; begins en algún momento, “at some point”
cards.noteEn: Here en introduces an indefinite point in time rather than a physical location.

example.en: We will discuss it at some point.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “at some point” without specifying when?
cards.noteEn: Algún comes before the masculine noun momento; the expression can refer to the past or future according to the verb.

example.en: We will see each other at some point.

cards.answerEn: some; some day/time (before a masculine noun)
cards.noteEn: Alguno shortens to algún directly before a masculine singular noun: algún día, algún libro.

example.en: Some neighbor will have the key.

cards.noteEn: Spanish writes de followed by the masculine singular word el as the single word del.

example.es: El color del coche es rojo.
example.en: The color of the car is red.

cards.answerEn: each other; marks a shared action involving “us”
cards.noteEn: With a plural verb, nos can show that the speakers do the action to or with each other. Context distinguishes this reciprocal use from nos meaning simply “us.”

example.en: We hugged each other.

cards.noteEn: Encontramos is the present form of encontrar for nosotros. With nos before it, nos encontramos can mean 'we meet each other.'

example.en: We meet at the station.

cards.noteEn: Before a specific moment, en can correspond to English “at.”

example.en: He arrived at just the right moment.

cards.noteEn: Ese points to a masculine singular noun that is not presented as right next to the speaker. Feminine singular is esa.

example.en: I do not recognize that sound.

cards.answerEn: Use he, has, ha, hemos, habéis, or han followed by the verb’s completed-action form.
cards.noteEn: These are forms of haber, the helper verb used here like English “have.” For most verbs, the completed-action form ends in -ado after an -ar verb and -ido after an -er or -ir verb. This form is called the past participle, and it does not change after haber. How often this tense is used instead of the simple past varies by region.
cards.questionEn: How do you say “have done,” as in “I have finished”?

example.en: I have finished.

cards.noteEn: Interactuado is the completed-action form of interactuar. It follows a form of haber, such as he, to say that an interaction has happened.

example.en: I have interacted with the system.

cards.questionEn: How do you name the person, system, or thing that someone interacts with?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of interactuar, then con, then name the other participant.
cards.noteEn: Interactuar changes for the person and time. Con is the required link to the other person or thing involved; English also normally uses 'with.'

example.es: Los clientes interactúan con la aplicación.
example.en: The customers interact with the application.

cards.questionEn: Why does the future punch request work like a deliberately self-hostile dead man's switch?
cards.answerEn: The speaker asks to be punched if he ever uses Klout for anything except removing himself, and he orders his friend to ignore any later attempt to cancel the instruction.
cards.noteEn: Klout was a service that assigned public social-influence scores. The speaker treats using it as shameful enough to justify a future punishment. A dead man's switch normally triggers when its operator stops actively preventing it; the title text jokingly applies that idea to a standing anti-Klout instruction that the speaker's future self cannot safely revoke, because every retraction must be ignored.

cards.answerEn: with; required before what someone interacts with
cards.noteEn: Interactuar normally uses con before the person, system, or thing involved in the interaction.

example.en: We interact with other teams.

cards.promptEs: persona o cosa no identificada + que + subjuntivo
cards.questionEn: How do you describe a person or thing whose existence or identity is not being treated as known?
cards.answerEn: Name the nonspecific person or thing, add que, and put the describing action in its special non-factual form.
cards.noteEn: That special form is called the subjunctive. It is useful after expressions such as cualquier or otra cosa when the speaker is not pointing to one established example. Compare busco un libro que explica esto, which describes a known book, with busco un libro que explique esto, where any suitable book would do.

example.es: Necesito a alguien que sepa francés.
example.en: I need someone who knows French.

cards.noteEn: Que connects a noun to information describing it. Depending on the noun, English translates it as “who,” “that,” or “which.”

example.es: La persona que llamó es mi amiga.
example.en: The person who called is my friend.

cards.answerEn: is; may be (a possibility form of ser)
cards.noteEn: Sea is a form of ser used when something is presented as uncertain, possible, desired, or otherwise not stated as a plain fact. For a straightforward statement, the corresponding form is es.

example.en: It may be true.

cards.answerEn: to remove myself; to delete my account or entry
cards.noteEn: Borrarme combines borrar with me. In a service or list context, it can mean removing one's own account, registration, or entry rather than literally erasing one's body.

example.en: I decided to remove myself from the list.

cards.questionEn: Where does me, te, se, nos, or os go when a verb used with one of those words stays in its dictionary form?
cards.answerEn: Attach the matching small word to the end: unir + me becomes unirme.
cards.noteEn: A pronominal verb is learned with se, such as unirse or acostarse. When its action verb remains in the unchanged dictionary form ending in -ar, -er, or -ir, replace se with the form that matches the person and write it as part of the same word: acostarme, unirte, or irnos.

example.en: I want to go to bed early.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that one person wants another person to do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of querer, then que, then put the other person's action in its special wanted-action form.
cards.noteEn: The special form is called the subjunctive. It appears because the second action is wanted, not stated as a fact. For example, ordinary tú das becomes quiero que tú des. If the same person wants to act, Spanish instead uses querer plus the unchanged dictionary form: quiero salir.

example.en: I want Ana to come tomorrow.

cards.noteEn: Que introduces a clause after verbs such as creer, saber, esperar, or decir. English often uses “that,” but may leave it unstated.

example.en: I think that Ana is coming.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone punches another person?
cards.answerEn: Use a matching form of dar, then un puñetazo, then a before the person punched.
cards.noteEn: Dar changes for the person and time, while un puñetazo names the blow. The a introduces the recipient of the blow. A short recipient word such as le can also mark that same person.

example.es: El boxeador dio un puñetazo a su rival.
example.en: The boxer punched his opponent.

cards.noteEn: Des is a special form of dar for one familiar listener. It appears after expressions of wanting, requesting, doubt, or possibility when the giving is not stated as a fact.

example.es: Quiero que me des una respuesta.
example.en: I want you to give me an answer.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone does one thing without doing another?
cards.answerEn: Put sin before the second action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: The dictionary form is the unchanged verb ending in -ar, -er, or -ir. When the same person performs both actions, Spanish uses sin directly before that form; it does not add a word equivalent to English “-ing.”

example.en: She left without closing the door.

cards.noteEn: Avisar means making someone aware beforehand or notifying them.

example.en: You should warn us before entering.

cards.noteEn: Esto is a neutral demonstrative for an unidentified thing, fact, or whole situation. It is not used directly before a noun.

example.en: This is difficult.

cards.noteEn: Te can mean “to you” when you are the recipient or the person affected by an action. It normally appears before a conjugated verb.

example.en: I’m sending you a message.

cards.answerEn: sounds; seems (before a comparison with a)
cards.noteEn: A form of sonar followed by a can compare the impression something gives with another thing.

example.en: That sounds like an excuse.

cards.questionEn: How do you say that something sounds like something else?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of sonar, then a, then the thing it resembles.
cards.noteEn: Sonar changes to match the person or thing producing the impression and the time: suena for one present thing, suenan for several. The word a stays unchanged before the comparison.

example.en: That plan sounds like a disaster.

cards.answerEn: like; required after sonar before the comparison
cards.noteEn: In sonar a algo, the preposition a links the impression to what it resembles.

example.en: The story sounds like a joke.

cards.noteEn: Broma is a humorous remark, trick, or prank; context distinguishes a spoken joke from an action played on someone.

example.en: It was an innocent joke.

cards.answerEn: I clarify; let me make clear
cards.noteEn: Aclaro is the present form of aclarar for the speaker. It often introduces a point meant to remove a possible misunderstanding.

example.es: Aclaro que no fue una crítica.
example.en: I clarify that it was not a criticism.

cards.answerEn: is; is meant (in va en serio)
no separate English word; part of en serio (“seriously”)

cards.questionEn: How do you ask whether someone is really serious or whether something is actually true?
cards.answerEn: Use en serio to mean “seriously,” “really,” or “for real.”
cards.noteEn: En serio is a fixed expression. In a question, ¿En serio? often reacts with surprise or disbelief; in a statement, it can contrast sincerity with joking.

example.en: Are you really going to run tomorrow?

cards.noteEn: Ignora is the affirmative command of ignorar for one familiar listener. The same spelling can also mean 'he, she, or it ignores,' so the surrounding instruction identifies the command.

example.en: Ignore that message.

cards.promptEs: orden afirmativa para tú: habla, come, escribe
cards.questionEn: How do you give one friend or familiar person a positive command?
cards.answerEn: Use the informal singular command form, often the same form used for “he” or “she” in the present.
cards.noteEn: For many regular verbs, -ar becomes -a and -er or -ir becomes -e: hablar becomes habla, comer becomes come, and escribir becomes escribe. Some common verbs are irregular or change their stem. Negative commands use a different form and are a separate pattern.

example.en: Open the window.

cards.questionEn: How do you say “any” before one singular thing?
cards.answerEn: Put cualquier before a singular noun: cualquier libro, cualquier opción.
cards.noteEn: A noun is a naming word such as libro or opción. Before a noun, cualquiera shortens to cualquier. The noun stays singular even when the meaning is any one out of many. The plus sign in the Spanish prompt means “followed by.”

example.en: You can choose any seat.

cards.noteEn: Una retractación is a later statement taking back or disowning an earlier claim, instruction, or accusation.

example.en: The newspaper published a retraction.

cards.answerEn: can (special form used when a possibility is not stated as a fact)
cards.noteEn: Pueda is a special form of poder, the verb meaning “can.” Spanish can use it after que when a description is uncertain, sought, or denied rather than presented as a fact. The ordinary statement form puede changes to pueda.

example.es: Busco a alguien que pueda ayudar.
example.en: I am looking for someone who can help.

cards.promptEs: poder + verbo en forma de diccionario
cards.questionEn: How do you say that someone can, could, or may do something?
cards.answerEn: Use a form of poder for the person and situation, then keep the action verb in its unchanged dictionary form.
cards.noteEn: Poder changes to forms such as puedo, puedes, puede, podemos, and pueden for present ability or possibility. Podría can present a possible or imagined option. The following action keeps its -ar, -er, or -ir ending.

example.en: We can enter now.
